fields.why: Single-group quantities are reported (inflammatory neurologic events in 3 of 17,922 and 3 of 20,255 vaccinees, with no comparator), so summary applies; B's quoted evidence (a VE estimate) is itself a comparison, though.
The article never states that a CI includes or excludes 1; 'similar' describes 4.4% vs 4.3% with the RR CI shown, so a CI-vs-fixed-value test is an inference, defensible but not explicit.
Same as procedure_classes: no explicit significance judgment; the coadministration noninferiority result is cited from references, not analyzed here.
Estimates carry CIs (some multiplicity-adjusted), but no test or explicit CI-vs-1 judgment is stated; B's 'CIs and tests' rests on reading 'similar' as a test.

Long-term care residence (older adults in a congregate setting, the brief's own example) is named only in a trial-enrollment limitation, so it can be recorded as a descriptor without raising the level; omitting it is also defensible because it is framed as a clinical risk factor.

brief_issues: Say whether a descriptive word such as 'similar' next to a ratio whose CI includes 1 counts as a CI-vs-fixed-value test.
